stories.source_title: Africa’s jobs problem is bigger than unemployment
stories.source_excerpt: With more than a third of employed Africans living in working poverty and 84.4% working informally, having a job does not necessarily mean earning enough to escape poverty or access social protection.
stories.headline: Beyond Unemployment: The Reality of Working Poverty in Africa
stories.dek: Recent reports indicate that standard employment metrics fail to capture the severe financial strain faced by millions of working Africans.
stories.body: When examining employment figures across the continent, traditional metrics of joblessness miss a critical part of the puzzle. According to insights shared by TechCabal in October 2026, the continent faces a much broader economic crisis defined by the quality of employment rather than the sheer lack of a job. Data reveals that more than one-third of employed individuals across the continent live in conditions of working poverty. This means that having a job does not guarantee financial security or a way out of impoverished conditions. Furthermore, the informal sector absorbs a staggering 84.4% of the workforce. Within this vast informal economy, workers typically lack access to formal social protections, leaving them vulnerable to economic shocks and systemic instability. As policymakers and analysts evaluate the path forward, these figures highlight that true economic progress requires tackling inadequate wages and informal vulnerabilities, not just creating baseline jobs.
